To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Pea protein isolates were successfully hydrolyzed with commercial proteases to produce antioxidant peptides.

the hydrolysate fraction of pea protein produced by Bacillus subtilas neutral protease at a dose of 250 and 500 μg/g beef exhibited significant inhibition against the oxidation of lipids during storage.
pea protein hydrolysates produced by commercial proteases and further purified by ultrafiltration can be used to inhibit lipid oxidation of meat products and improve their shelf-life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and natural antioxidants for meat and meat products.
the preparation and characterization of novel peptides from pea protein with strong antioxidative activities and their potential application as natural antioxidants in food.
the development of novel antioxidative peptides from pea protein isolate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antioxidative peptides derived and purified from pea protein isolate by proteolytic hydrolysis and ultrafiltration are promising alternatives to synthetic antioxidants for the prevention of lipid oxidation and the improvement of shelf-life in lipid-rich foods.

the hydrolysates prepared from pea proteins using commercial proteases and sequential ultrafiltration have strong antioxidative activities and can effectively inhibit lipid oxidation in meat products during storage.
the specific antioxidation hydrolysates prepared from pea protein with the combination of commercial protease and ultrafiltration could be used to improve shelf life of lipid-rich food.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient and cost-effective method to obtain antioxidative hydrolysate from pea protein isolate.

the antioxidative hydrolysate produced from pea protein by the commercial protease from Bacillis subtilis and ultrafiltration (NP-F4) was found to have a significant inhibitory effect on lipid oxidation in ground beef, which was comparable to that of butylated hydroxyl anisole, a commonly used synthetic antioxidative agent.
pea protein isolate is an excellent source for producing antioxidative peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pea protein can be used to produce antioxidant peptides that can be applied to meat to improve shelf life and prevent lipid oxidation.
the antioxidative peptides derived by hydrolysis of pea protein isolates with commercial microbial proteases can be used to inhibit lipid oxidation in food systems.

the specific antioxidive peptides produced from pea protein hydrolysates with commercial proteases, and ultrafiltration, could be used to inhibit lipid oxidation, and improve shelf-life, of lipid-rich food.
